chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

About a man who is affected by janābah during a cold night and fears destruction for himself if he performs ghusl, so he said: "He performs tayammum and prays; then when he is safe from the cold, he performs ghusl and repeats the salat."

key_terms.اغْتَسَلَ: he performs ghusl, the ritual bath
key_terms.التَّلَفَ: serious harm or destruction feared for oneself
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the ritual prayer to be performed and then repeated
key_terms.اللَّيْلَةِ الْبَارِدَةِ: a cold night in which use of water may cause harm
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةُ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum as a substitute for wudu or ghusl when water use is harmful

ai.seo_question: What should a junub person do if extreme cold makes ghusl dangerous?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one in a state of janābah who fears harm from using water in severe cold. He should perform tayammum and offer the prayer, then later perform ghusl and repeat the prayer once the danger has passed.
